I'm pretty much a noob, but I'd think the lower CAS latency would be the better choice.

Lower CAS/timing is better, yes. However, 32GB of RAM is massive overkill for a gaming rig. Even 16GB is overkill, but more than enough unless you're doing a ton of editing or the most extreme of multi-tasking.

If you're set on 32GB, buy this RAM. Cheaper and faster. Note that higher frequency/lower CAS isn't going to make a difference for gaming, though. It barely makes any difference at all, except for editing (but even that is minimal).

I'll also occasionally be using this for graphic design, but usually only Illustrator, InDesign and Photoshop simultaneously.

It's really good to know that that much RAM won't make a big difference. The Ares set kept coming up when I was looking for RAM, but I never looked into it. Thanks a ton for pointing me towards it.

Yes, lower CAS is better (the first number in those sequences is the CAS latency). CAS latency is how long it takes to process a request, so lower is better.

Also, I agree with /u/AmyAcker that 32GB (and probably even 16GB) is overkill for a gaming rig. If you're trying to cut costs you'll be fine with 8GB and then if you need it, buy another stick or two.
